commits.title: chore(git): define archive boundaries for acquisition data and runtimes
commits.description:
Define ignore rules for local raw corpora, databases, API responses, repeated large inventories, runtime dependencies and temporary files while retaining reports, code and existing hash receipts.

Document recovery boundaries between Git and local evidence. Retain one public robots snapshot required by the network-denied fixtures. Ignore rules delete no evidence and do not alter tracked content or the independent audit seal.

commits.title: docs(research): fix the publication interval and staged research rules
commits.description:
Archive project instructions, direction and methodological decisions with the publication interval fixed at 1988-01-01 through 2026-09-21; September remains partial.

Place distribution, source and structural checks before climate retrieval, affect associations and fear interpretation, with RQ1/RQ2 first. Preserve regional sources, native units and denominators without requiring exhaustive countries, uniform volume or fear words.

Update README and architecture navigation without rewriting frozen pilot labels or the submitted proposal.

commits.title: docs(proposal): archive proposal versions, references and figure materials
commits.description:
Archive existing proposal text, historical versions, references, method and sampling discussions, figure sources and build scripts, generated PDFs and figure-check evidence.

Retain original dates, review decisions and submission versions. This archival step does not regenerate figures, run statistics or revise the submitted proposal. Course originals and local Python runtimes remain outside Git.

commits.title: docs(pilot): archive acquisition pilots and meeting deliverables
commits.description:
Preserve feasibility meeting summaries, reports and build scripts, the NLP handoff and initial batch request-status inventories.

Distinguish existing reports, successes, failures and unattempted records. Raw bodies, databases and bulk exports remain local. Archiving neither launches downloads nor turns historical plans into acquired text.

commits.title: feat(coverage): archive regional government source and temporal frames
commits.description:
Archive official source enumeration, month/year indexes, original manifests, availability reports and coverage-figure scripts.

Preserve US/AU/EU and IE/NZ assessments and acquisition handoffs with source, genre and native Work/parent/question units. API responses, complete row inventories and raw PDFs remain local. Monthly presence does not establish full text or comparable emotion series.

commits.title: feat(acquisition): archive US and AU historical original routes
commits.description:
Preserve US/AU download and parsing code, historical issue discovery, GovInfo fallback, AU original triage, source throttling and coverage summaries.

Retain source registers, filter contracts, route exceptions and run instructions. Historical scans, OCR and original availability retain their recorded limits. This archival step restarts no stopped route, downloads no full issue and changes no formal database; raw and bulk reports stay local.

commits.title: feat(cellar): archive the EU Work and Item acquisition pipeline
commits.description:
Preserve CELLAR monthly Work enumeration, WEMI relation parsing, Item download/staging, OCR candidates and object-specific persistent stops.

Archive runbooks and compact evidence with the existing source classes, English Expressions and Work/Manifestation/Item boundaries. The historical 50,578-Work metadata frame is not an equal number of complete bodies. Candidate, component, OCR and no-link states retain their separate meanings and frozen denominators.

commits.title: docs(pilot): freeze Paris-window readiness and diagnostic evidence
commits.description:
Preserve the 49-month three-role readiness table, government diagnostic sample, Guardian date/month frames and petition checks, including the second-round published-petition date correction.

These are historical bounded samples and discovery frames. Bodies and pilot climate/fear labels are not retrospectively changed or adopted as current exclusion rules. Local three-role overlap does not establish a comparable complete monthly panel.

commits.title: feat(eda): archive distribution snapshots and historical figures
commits.description:
Preserve EDA preparation, graph construction, source tables, figure checks and coverage snapshots, including four existing high-resolution lexical inventory figures.

Historical lexical/Ngram measures, query hits, source-record coverage and validated evidence retain their own units. They are not combined into climate or fear prevalence. Snapshot dates and limits remain unchanged; Git archiving reruns no plotting or cleaning.

commits.title: feat(audit): archive date, distribution and source-quality diagnostics
commits.description:
Archive three structural diagnostic packages for the fixed cutoff, source/genre/month counts and source quality, including executable diagnostics, checkpoints, reports and coordinator corrections.

Keep technical status, directness, date/identity mapping and unverified coverage distinct. Preserve legitimate high-volume periods and mirror/shared-source limits. Historical diagnostics are not rerun or used as entropy, climate or fear cleaning thresholds.

commits.title: feat(validation): archive the archive-reply split validator
commits.description:
Preserve independent reply-split validation, punctuation/date-range/HTML boundary checks, targeted fixtures, compact results and exception inventories.

Separate independent parents, shared reply groups, containers and raw boundaries; distinguish legitimate sharing from duplication. Large parent results and repeated full-pass snapshots remain local, traceable through original manifests and hashes. No new archive scan or universal exception resolution is claimed.

commits.title: feat(provenance): archive source, date and version validators
commits.description:
Preserve provenance/date logic validation, rule dictionaries, applicability, annotated exceptions and targeted tests. Archive the two structural validators' scope, shared I/O-lock protocol and coordinator acceptance.

Validate identity, publication/version time, parent relationships and source eras without equating provenance with the truth of every statement. Repair and backfill follow acceptance; large row-level findings remain local.

commits.title: fix(corpus): archive accepted parent repairs and transaction evidence
commits.description:
Preserve the existing repair CLI, conservation checks, HTML group retention, date intervals and source exceptions, together with single-writer application, lease/transaction checkpoints and coordinator acceptance.

Accepted UK effective parents remain 248,319, with 248,268 month-assignable. Preserve 318 unresolved issue instances across 165 units and adapter limits. These are accepted evidence counts; this archival step reruns no repair, writes no database and clears no unresolved state.

Large repair plans and historical copies remain local; Git retains code, dispositions, scope and application evidence.

commits.title: feat(supplement): freeze EU candidates and original-request queues
commits.description:
Preserve targeted original requests, EU2015 candidate selection, frozen coordinates and Work/Item relation evidence, including five final original targets and 979 selected Item targets.

The 979 count is a target denominator, not complete Works or successful bodies. No-link and multi-Item/component states within 1,009 Works retain their meanings. This archival step expands no queue, launches no backfill and writes no formal database.

commits.title: docs(analysis): archive repair checkpoints and audit-sealing boundaries
commits.description:
Archive existing post-repair status reports, recommendations, evidence manifests and check results, plus the public independent-audit handoff and encryption decision.

Reuse accepted government aggregates and change records rather than repeating a whole-corpus scan. Reviewer source, hidden fixtures, encrypted archives and credentials remain outside Git. Collectors receive factual issues and input/output receipts only. Retain the historical acquisition-audit workbook and exclude temporary inspection dumps.

commits.title: fix(downloader): archive bounded transport repairs and stop states
commits.description:
Preserve downloader release-schema adaptation, stage A before B, offline transport fixtures, original-request ledgers and the frozen EU Item staging handoff, including before/after source and version receipts.

Retain the historical original HTTP403/unattempted outcomes and EU stop after 20 saved Items with the 21st returning406. This precedes the later continuation and does not claim 979 completion. Raw/partial accounting, rate limits, shared lock and original budget bounds remain applicable.

commits.title: feat(gov): archive government closeout, independent metrics and four figures
commits.description:
Archive the evidenced transport continuation, frozen government input, changed-Item local checks, independent distribution tables, four figures, closeout report and coordinator acceptance.

Final staging is 47/979 candidate Items, 45 distinct raw hashes and 22,231,574 bytes; one current406 and931 unattempted remain, with zero new originals among five targets. Historical stops persist; complete Work or full-year collection is not claimed and no formal import occurs.

Interpret entropy/HHI within declared source frames, distinguish unknown coverage from evidenced zeros and retain Item lengths as file diagnostics. The evaluator remains sealed outside the repository; Git holds public results and receipts only.

commits.title: feat(media): archive five-region schema and precollection design
commits.description:
Preserve EU/Europe, UK, AU, US and NZ media/newspaper design at 30 original slots each, source/era access tables, field dictionary, schema, prototype and immutable V1/V2 receipts.

Keep edition-scoped article identity, publication instances, bylines/quoted speakers, versions, issue/OCR, licences and unknown denominators separate. The 37 existing offline checks support the prototype; new real articles/full bodies remain zero. A 212-byte challenge is not an article and no bulk collection starts automatically.

commits.title: fix(media): preserve persistent data and strengthen source-version constraints
commits.description:
Archive repairs for persistent databases, transaction rollback, slot/frame source-edition constraints, same-parent versions, candidate mappings and full-body offline checks, with explicit scope/digest release and the final 150-row ledger.

The coordinator reran 19 network-denied targeted checks and one temporary whole-chain scenario successfully; five simulated articles never entered real outputs. Actual requests produced four policy objects and one empty date search; body requests, article parents, versions, full bodies, issues and OCR remain zero, with all 150 original slots unfilled.

An empty search does not establish zero monthly publication. First publication, article rights exceptions, complete boundaries and historical versions still require real payloads. Both owner turns ended without deadline extension; government database and sealed evaluator access remain zero.

commits.title: docs(notebook): archive the synthetic end-to-end demonstration
commits.description:
Preserve added code, explanatory and output cells in the existing synthetic end-to-end notebook.

Validate notebook JSON and Python cell syntax without rerunning models or acquiring external data. The demonstration checks software interfaces and workflow paths; it is not a historical-corpus result or a completed real media-body pipeline.

commits.title: docs(history): index the archived outcomes and project log
commits.description:
Archive the project-stage log and decision navigation with the outcome-based commit index.

The original index records 20 preceding commit identifiers and this 21st archival step. Messages retain real multiline titles/descriptions, changes, existing evidence and unresolved limits. The later English-message integration supplies a separate identifier map while preserving these frozen files.

Original archival timestamps are retained. Raw corpora, large databases, local dependencies, temporary files and sealed reviewer credentials remain outside Git.
